found through a helper, no traffic yet

The edgevpn node is running and has an open libp2p connection to at least one peer listed in the network\'s machines ledger.
The VPN is on, but none of your devices has been reached yet. On mobile data this can take a few minutes.
The node is running and searching the public DHT for peers under the network\'s rendezvous point, and listening for mDNS on Wi-Fi. No machine in the ledger has an open connection yet.

The VPN could not start, or stopped because of an error.
Error details is the exact error, as returned by the step that failed. It is left out when the error could contain part of the network key; the logs still have it.
The address your other devices use to reach this phone inside your network.
The IPv4 address of the phone\'s VPN (TUN) interface, announced in the machines ledger.
How this phone is connected to the internet right now.
The transport of the active underlying network, from Android\'s ConnectivityManager.
The devices that have joined your network with the same network key.
Entries of the machines bucket in the edgevpn ledger, which every node keeps a copy of and syncs over GossipSub.
This phone and the device talk straight to each other. This is the fastest way.
At least one open libp2p connection to the peer is not relayed (no /p2p-circuit in the remote multiaddr) and not limited.

Your phone and this device found each other through another computer on the internet that offered to help, but they can\'t reach each other directly yet, usually because both are behind a home router or a mobile network. The VPN sends nothing through helpers, so no traffic passes between the two until they open a direct path. They keep trying while the VPN is on.

The only connections are libp2p circuit relay v2 connections (limited; the multiaddr contains /p2p-circuit). edgevpn opens its VPN and ledger streams without allowing limited connections, so libp2p waits for a direct connection from hole punching (DCUtR) or connection reversal, for up to the 15 s frame timeout, and drops the packet when none appears. Public relays also limit these connections (default: 2 minutes, 128 KiB).
The device is in your network but can\'t be reached right now. It may be switched off or without internet.
The peer is in the machines ledger but there is no open libp2p connection to it. \"Last seen\" comes from its last health check in the ledger.
Same Wi-Fi or over the internet
Whether the device is on the same local network as this phone.
Same Wi-Fi means the remote IP of the direct connection is a private address in the same subnet as one of the phone\'s Wi-Fi addresses. Otherwise the connection goes over the internet.
How well this phone can find your devices on the internet.
Discovery uses the public libp2p DHT (Kademlia) and, on Wi-Fi, mDNS.
Other computers on the internet this phone is talking to. They help your devices find each other and set up direct connections. Your VPN traffic never passes through them.
Number of connected libp2p peers that are not machines of the network: DHT servers, relays and bootstrap nodes.
How long ago any of your devices last checked in.
The newest health check timestamp written to the ledger by another node (edgevpn\'s Alive service, every 2 minutes).
The secret that lets devices join your network. Anyone who has it can join, so keep it private.

The edgevpn network token: base64-encoded YAML holding the room name, the rendezvous string, two OTP keys (one rotates the DHT rendezvous point, one encrypts the messages between nodes), the mDNS service name and the maximum message size.
What your other devices see as this phone\'s name.
The Hostname field of this phone\'s entry in the machines ledger.
The address your other devices use to reach this phone inside your network.
The IPv4 address of the phone\'s VPN (TUN) interface, announced in the machines ledger. The VPN routes the address with a /24 mask through the tunnel.
Writes much more detail to the logs, to help find problems. Uses more battery, so turn it off when done.
Sets the edgevpn log level to debug and the libp2p log level to debug. libp2p\'s lines go to logcat (tag GoLog), not to the in-app logs.

Lets other devices on the internet pass the start of a connection through this phone, so that two devices behind home routers can find a direct path to each other. Any device that uses the same peer-to-peer system (libp2p) can use it, not only yours. It uses some data and battery. Each relayed connection is cut after 2 minutes or 128 KB, whichever comes first. It only works while this phone can be reached from the internet, for example on some Wi-Fi networks with IPv6.

Runs the libp2p circuit relay v2 service with go-libp2p\'s default limits: 128 KiB per direction and 2 minutes per relayed connection, 16 circuits per peer, 128 reservations, a reservation TTL of 1 hour and a 2048 byte buffer per circuit. go-libp2p starts the service only while AutoNAT reports the phone as publicly reachable. Any peer may reserve a slot; there is no check that it belongs to your network. The service starts with the VPN, so a change applies after a reconnect.
A unique identifier for this phone in your network.
The libp2p peer ID, derived from the phone\'s Ed25519 identity key. It signs this phone\'s ledger entries.
Makes this phone forget everything and start over as a new device.

Another device in your network has the same address as this phone. Your network keeps only one device per address, so your other devices can\'t see this phone until one of the two moves to another address.

Within the last minute this phone rejected a machines ledger entry for its own address, sent by another peer. An entry belongs to the peer that wrote it while that peer\'s heartbeat is fresh (the ownership TTL, 8 minutes by default), so each of the two devices keeps its own entry and rejects the other\'s, and both show this warning. It can also show for up to the TTL after Start fresh, while other devices still hold the old identity\'s entry.

The Wi-Fi or wired network you are on uses addresses in the same range as your VPN. While the VPN is on, the phone sends everything for that range into the VPN, so devices on this network with those addresses, such as a printer or the router, may not answer. Your other devices on this network also reach this phone through the internet instead of directly. To fix it, move your VPN network to a range this network does not use, or change the range of this network in its router.

A Wi-Fi or Ethernet network this phone is connected to has an IPv4 prefix that overlaps the /24 the VPN routes into the tunnel, the /24 of this phone\'s VPN address. Traffic for that /24 goes into the tunnel, and the phone leaves addresses inside it out of the addresses it advertises to peers, so peers on the same network cannot dial it directly. Every device in an edgevpn network uses the same /24, so the fix is a new range for all of them. Mobile data is not checked. Which route Android picks for a LAN address inside the VPN range is untested.

Deletes the network token, the Ed25519 identity key (so a new peer ID is generated) and all settings and logs. The old ledger entries stay owned by the old identity until the ownership TTL (8 minutes) expires.
